checks.do: Whether a change to a standard report was made on a copy, since standard reports cannot be edited.
Whether deleting a custom report also removed a schedule or a favorite that someone depends on, since deleted reports cannot be restored.
When a scheduled report is sent and who can open its link, which the pages describe two ways.
Whether a filter change after scheduling is what changed the content recipients receive.

custom-limit-500.statement: An organization can create up to 500 custom reports, shared across all administrators, and each report can display up to 20 widgets.

quotes: An organization can create up to 500 custom reports shared across all administrators.
Each report can display up to 20 widgets.

standard-not-editable.statement: Standard reports cannot be deleted or edited; to change one, copy it, which creates a new custom report, and edit the copy.

quotes: Standard reports cannot be deleted.
Admins can only edit custom reports. Standard reports cannot be edited.
To edit a standard report, you can copy it, and then edit it.
Copying a standard report allows you to create a new custom report.

owner-or-super-admin.statement: Admins with the default super admin role can edit or delete any custom report; all other admins can edit or delete only their own.

quotes: Admins with the default super admin role can delete any report; all other admins can only delete their own reports.
Admins with the default super admin role can edit any custom report; all other admins can only edit their own reports.

delete-cascades.statement: Deleting a custom report also removes it from Favorites, and deletes its schedule if it was scheduled; deleted reports cannot be restored.

quotes: If the report was in the Favorites tab, it is deleted from there as well. Additionally, if it was a scheduled report, its schedule is deleted as well.
Deleted reports cannot be restored.

favorites-50.statement: Each admin can favorite up to 50 reports.

quotes: you have starred as your favorites. Each admin can favorite up to 50 reports.

custom-time-frame.statement: A custom report time frame cannot start before January 1, 2012 and spans at most 90 days; selecting multiple days shows the sum of bytes or transactions per day in charts.

quotes: The start date cannot be earlier than January 1, 2012.
The maximum time range is 90 days.
Selecting multiple days results in seeing the sum of bytes/transactions per day in charts.

per-widget-time.statement: When creating a report, the time frame can be set for all widgets or for each widget separately, and this option can be changed at any time.

quotes: You can set the time frame for all widgets in your report or select Allow time to be set for each widget to set a different time frame for each widget. You can change this option at any time.

title-75.statement: A report title must be unique and can contain up to 75 characters.

quotes: The report title must be unique, and it can contain up to 75 characters.

data-classes.statement: A new report is created under a report data class; the page lists Firewall, Endpoint DLP (EDLP), Email DLP and Combined among the classes, and says reports can cover web traffic, mobile traffic or a combination of both.

quotes: choose the report data class you want your report to fall under, and click OK:
you can create reports that provide information about web, mobile traffic, or a combination of both.
- Firewall
- Endpoint DLP (EDLP)
- Email DLP
- Combined

filter-narrowing.statement: Some data types are mutually exclusive between report-level and widget-level filters; for example, a Department filter at the report level removes Location at the widget level.

quotes: Some data types are mutually exclusive, so you can't see all the data types all the time.
For example, if you set the Department filter at the report level, Location is no longer available at the widget level.

top-threat-names-excluded.statement: The widgets for the Top Threat Names report cannot be used in custom reports.

quotes: The widgets for the report Top Threat Names cannot be used in custom reports.

top-five-other.statement: A widget displays the top five items and groups everything else under Other.

quotes: A widget displays the top five items and groups everything else under Other.

view-logs-not-for-samples.statement: The View Logs option is not available for charts that display secure browsing class, data or status, because those charts only use samples as their data units.

quotes: Click the View Logs option to view the chart’s logs in the Insights Logs page.
This option is not available for charts that display secure browsing class, data or status, because they only use samples as their data units.

export-import-json.statement: Only custom reports can be exported, to a plain-text JSON file that includes the report definitions (to export a standard report, copy it first). Only JSON files exported from the Zscaler Admin Console can be imported, and with more than one organization a report exported from one can be imported into another.

quotes: You can export custom reports to a plain-text JSON file that includes the report definitions.
The reports use a custom data structure, so you can only import JSON files that were exported from the Zscaler Admin Console.
You can export custom reports only. To export a standard report, you can copy it, and then export it.
if you have more than one organization, you can export a report from one organization and import it into another.

duplicate-by-editing-json.statement: The page's procedure for duplicating a report edits the exported JSON file in a text editor and changes the report's user name and title.

quotes: Using a text editor, such as Notepad, edit the JSON file.
Change the user name and title of the report.

print-view.statement: Any standard or custom report can be printed from Print View; some settings, such as printing to PDF, depend on the OS and browser.

quotes: You can print any standard or custom report. The service provides a Print View mode where you can view a report and then print it.
Some settings, such as the ability to print to PDF, depend on your OS and browser.

exclude-location.statement: User-related widgets include locations and users by default. The Exclude Location filter applies to all user-related widgets except those in the default Security dashboard, and also to the Executive Report and all standard, user-related reports in Interactive Reports.

quotes: By default, user-related widgets include locations and users.
This filter applies to all user-related widgets except for widgets in the default Security dashboard.
Excluding locations also applies to the Executive Report and all standard, user-related reports in Interactive Reports.

schedule-limit-500.statement: An organization can schedule up to 500 reports, and a report can be associated with many schedules, for example when a super admin schedules the same reports for department managers in different time zones.

quotes: An organization can schedule up to 500 reports. A report can be associated with many schedules.
This is useful, for example, when a super admin wants to schedule the same reports for various department managers in different time zones.

schedule-uses-current-parameters.statement: A scheduled report always reflects the current parameters of the report that is scheduled.

quotes: The scheduled report always reflects the current parameters of the report that is scheduled.

schedule-links.statement: Scheduled reports are emailed to the recipients as links; when a recipient clicks the link, the report appears in Print View. The link is valid for 15 days only.

quotes: The scheduled reports are emailed as links to the recipients. When the recipients click the link, they see the report in Print View.
The link is valid for 15 days only.

schedule-ownership.statement: A super admin can view and edit all scheduled reports; other administrators can view and manage only their own scheduled reports.

quotes: A super admin can view and edit all scheduled reports. Other administrators can view and manage their own scheduled reports only.

recipients-32.statement: A schedule sends the report to up to 32 email addresses, each on a separate line.

quotes: Each email address must be on a separate line. You can send the report to up to 32 email addresses.

frequency-semantics.statement: Daily gives the report for the previous day from 12:00:00 AM to 11:59:00 PM; Monthly delivers it on the first day of every month; the schedule's Time Zone is the one the service uses when it generates the report.

quotes: Select Daily if you want the report for the previous day from 12:00:00 AM to 11:59:00 PM.
Select Monthly if you want the report delivered to the specified recipients on the first day of every month.
Time Zone: Choose the time zone that the service uses when it generates the report.

daily-link-fixed-interval.statement: For a daily report, the link displays the report for the time interval for which the report was scheduled.

quotes: For a daily report, the link displays the report for the time interval for which the report was scheduled.

recipients-view-only.statement: Recipients can only view the report; they cannot edit it or navigate to any other area of the Zscaler Admin Console.

quotes: Recipients can only view the report; they cannot edit it or navigate to any other area of the Zscaler Admin Console.

weekly-delivery-time.summary: The Scheduling Reports page says Weekly delivery is every Monday at 9:00 AM, and the same page lists a Sent at field for the time the report is sent.

quotes: Select Weekly if you want the report delivered to the specified recipients every Monday at 9:00 AM.

positions.says: A Weekly schedule delivers the report every Monday at 9:00 AM.

quotes: Sent at: The time at which the report is to be sent.

positions.says: Sent at is the time at which the report is to be sent, without saying it does not apply to Weekly.

weekly-delivery-time.impact: Whether an administrator can choose the time of a Weekly schedule, or it always goes Monday at 9:00 AM, is not settled by the page. The Sandbox weekly-email pages are a different report type.

link-access.summary: The Scheduling Reports page says anyone with a scheduled report's link can access the report, and also that a recipient who pastes the URL must log in to the Admin Console.

quotes: Anyone who has the link can access the report. The link is valid for 15 days only.

positions.says: Anyone who has the link can access the report; the link is valid for 15 days only.

quotes: If a recipient copies and pastes the report URL, the Zscaler Admin Console login page appears and the recipient is required to enter a valid user name and password to log in.

positions.says: A recipient who copies and pastes the report URL gets the Admin Console login page and must enter a valid user name and password.

link-access.impact: Whether a scheduled-report link is usable by a person with no Admin Console account is not settled by the page.

export-schema.title: What the exported report JSON contains
export-schema.detail: The Exporting and Importing page says the file includes the report definitions and uses a custom data structure. The schema is not documented in the captured pages.

widget-types.title: Widget types, data types and per-widget limits
widget-types.detail: The pages refer to About Widgets and Analyzing Traffic Using Insights, which are not captured in this area, so widget types, data types and per-widget limits beyond the 20-widget cap are undefined here.

schedule-status-values.title: Scheduled-report Status values and data retention
schedule-status-values.detail: The captured pages do not list the Status values of a scheduled report or say how far back report data exists beyond the January 1, 2012 start-date floor.

data-class-short-items.title: The Web, Mobile and DNS data classes
data-class-short-items.detail: The Creating or Copying a Report list has Web, Mobile and DNS items that are too short to quote alone, so the data-classes claim quotes the other items and the opening sentence about web and mobile traffic.
